(لا) is negative, (يسمعون) is an imperfect verb and the wāw is an agent. (فيها) is a pair attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "in their state of being in the Garden". (لغوا) is a direct object, meaning speech with no substance, which is what most people prattle in their gatherings of backbiting others and meddling in people's affairs, or trivial talk akin to idle meddling. (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (سلاما) is a badal from (لغوا), or is taken as a discontinuous exception, the detail of which will come in the section on Rhetoric. (لهم) is a fronted khabar and (رزقهم) a postponed mubtadaʾ. (فيها) is a ḥāl. (بكرة) is an adverb attached to the sense of residence latent in the fronted khabar, and (عشيا) is conjoined to (بكرة).
(تِلْكَ الْجَنَّةُ الَّتِي نُورِثُ مِنْ عِبادِنا مَنْ كانَ تَقِيًّا): The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and (الجنة) is the khabar. (التي) is an adjective of (الجنة). The clause (نورث) is the ṣila. (من) is a relative noun, the object of (نورث). The clause (كان) is the ṣila, the noun of (كان) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", and (تقيا) is the predicate of (كان). «[Translator's note: the source says «وجملة تقيا خبر كان», "the clause (تقيا)"; (تقيا) is a single word, not a clause, so the intended sense is "(تقيا) is the predicate of (كان)".]»

* Rhetoric:
1- Confirming praise by what resembles blame, and the reverse:
In His saying «لا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيها لَغْواً إِلَّا سَلاماً» there is a lofty art among the arts of rhetoric, namely confirming praise by what resembles blame. It was pointed out earlier in al-Māʾida, but we did not divide it then, so we say that it divides into two types:
A- That an attribute of praise of that thing be excepted from a negated attribute of blame, on the assumption that it is included in the negated blame attribute. An example is the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم ... بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب
(There is no fault in them except that their swords have notches from battering the battalions.)
He made the notches a fault only figuratively, in order to establish the total negation of fault, as if saying: if the notching of a sword from striking is a fault, then they have a fault; its meaning is that if it is not a fault, then there is no fault in them at all, since there is nothing besides this. So after this figurative supposition it is a continuous exception.
B- That an attribute of praise be affirmed of something and followed by a particle of exception followed by another attribute of praise of that thing, such as: "I am the most eloquent of the Arabs, except that I am from Quraysh." Al-Nābigha also said:
فتى كملت أوصافه غير أنه ... جواد فما يبقي على المال باقيا
(A youth whose qualities are perfected, except that he is so generous that he leaves nothing of his wealth.)
The origin of the exception in this type is that it is discontinuous, but it is not assumed continuous; it remains discontinuous, because in this type there is no general negated blame attribute into which one could suppose the praise attribute to enter. Then the confirmation is not obtained except from the second of the two aspects mentioned in the first type. For this reason the first type is more eloquent, as it gives confirmation from both aspects.
When you know this, know that in the noble verse «لا يسمعون فيها لغوا إلا سلاما» there are three aspects: A- Its meaning is that if their greeting one another, or the angels' greeting, is considered idle talk, then they hear no idle talk except that; and so it is of the same kind as the saying of al-Nābigha: «ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم ... بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب». B- That they hear in it only speech in which they are safe from fault and defect, and here the exception must be discontinuous. C- That the meaning of salām is the supplication for safety, and it is the abode of safety whose people have no need of supplication for safety, so its outward form would be idle and excess talk were it not for the benefit of honouring. In the first and third aspects the exception must be continuous. As for the first, it is because that is made idle talk by way of figure and supposition; as for the second (sic), it is clear, because in it the word "idle talk" is applied to salām; and as for the third, it is because the speech is taken at its apparent sense without figure or supposition. «[Translator's note: the source's final summary assigns "continuous" to the first and third aspects, but then calls the middle justification «الثاني» ("the second") although the aspect it describes (applying "idle talk" to salām) is the third; the ordering in the source is kept as written.]»

2- The eloquent comparison by representation (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī):
That is in His saying «تِلْكَ الْجَنَّةُ الَّتِي نُورِثُ مِنْ عِبادِنا مَنْ كانَ تَقِيًّا». He likened the bestowal of the Garden on them to the bestowal that is not taken back, namely the inheritance which the heir inherits, which the one bequeathing does not retract. That is, We leave it to them as the fruit of their piety, as the heir is left the wealth of the one he inherits from. Inheritance (wirātha) is the strongest word used for conveying ownership and entitlement, in that it is not followed by cancellation or recovery, and is not voided by rejection or waiver. Irth in the language means remaining. He, upon him be blessings and peace, said: «You are on an irth from the irth of your father Ibrahim», that is, on a remnant of the remnants of his law. And al-Wārith (the Inheritor) is one of the names of Allah the Exalted, that is, the Remaining after the passing of His creation. In the Sharia it is the transfer of another's property to another by way of succession.

dervis-irab:64-65.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما نَتَنَزَّلُ إِلَّا بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ): The clause is resumptive, introduced to report the words of Jibril when the Messenger, upon him be peace, felt that he was slow, after being asked about the story of the People of the Cave, Dhu al-Qarnayn and the spirit, and did not know what to answer, as was mentioned earlier. He was slow in coming to him for fifteen days, and it is said forty, until the polytheists said: "His Lord has left him and hates him." The wāw is resumptive, (ما) is negative, (نتنزل) is an imperfect nominative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "we". (إلا بأمر ربك) is an exception from the most general of circumstances: (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (بأمر) is a pair attached to an omitted ḥāl. Tanazzul is a descent involving slowness, or it is in the sense of descent in general. The poet said:
فلست لإنسيّ ولكن لملأك ... تنزل من جو السماء يصوب
(You are not for a human but for an angel, who comes down from the air of the sky, aiming.)
This verse is by a man of ʿAbd al-Qays praising King al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir; it is also said to be by Abu Wajra praising ʿAbdallah ibn al-Zubayr, and before it is: «تعاليت ان تعزى إلى الانس جلة ... وللإنس من يعزوك فهو كذوب» (You are too exalted to be ascribed to humankind en masse; whoever ascribes you to humans is a liar.) That is, you are not attributed to a human but to an angel, and he exaggerated in that until he made him descending from the direction of the sky, yaṣūb, that is, aiming at a particular direction. Al-malʾak is, according to the source, maʿfal with the ʿayn fronted, from al-alūka with fatḥa, which means a message; Abu ʿUbayda said it is mafʿal, a noun of place from laʾaka when he sent, and perhaps it came on mafʿal to depict the messenger as the place of the message; Ibn Kaysān said it is faʿʾal from al-malak, so the hamza is redundant. In any case it is lightened by transfer, so one says malak. «[Translator's note: the source says «معفل بتقديم العين» (maʿfal, with the ʿayn fronted), a description of the metathesis of malʾak from maʾlak/laʾaka, kept as written.]»
(لَهُ ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِينا وَما خَلْفَنا وَما بَيْنَ ذلِكَ): (له) is a fronted khabar, (ما) is a relative, a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl from (ربك). The adverbial is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative. (أيدينا) is annexed to the adverbial. (وما خلفنا) is conjoined to (ما بين أيدينا), and (وما بين ذلك) is likewise conjoined.
(وَما كانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا): The wāw is a conjunction, (ما) is negative, with (كان), its noun and its predicate.
(رَبُّ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما): (رب السموات والأرض) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth"; it may also be parsed as a badal from (ربك).
(فَاعْبُدْهُ وَاصْطَبِرْ لِعِبادَتِهِ هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيًّا): The fāʾ is the "eloquent" fāʾ, and there is no need to reinterpret the speech by making it a conjunction, as a case of conjoining a performative sentence to a declarative one: that is, "If you have known His perfect lordship, then worship Him". (اصطبر) is conjoined to (اعبده). (لعبادته) is a pair attached to (اصطبر). Al-Zamakhsharī did well in his understanding, making worship like an opponent in combat: you say to the fighter "iṣṭabir li-qarnika", that is, stand firm against him in what he brings upon you of his onslaughts and assaults. What is meant is: do not be hard-pressed or weak in strength if revelation is delayed from you, and do not be distressed at the gloating of the unbelievers, for it is only a deluge and then it clears, a darkness and then it recedes. (هل) is an interrogative particle whose meaning is negation. (تعلم) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you". (سميا) is a direct object; al-samiyy is the one who shares the name.

* Benefits:
Conjoining a performative sentence to a declarative one and the reverse:
The rhetoricians and some of the grammarians forbade it, and some grammarians allowed it. Abū Ḥayyān said:
Sībawayh allowed that and cited as evidence the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وإن شفائي عبرة مهراقة ... وهل عند رسم دارس من معول
(My cure is a tear poured out; but is there any reliance on an effaced trace?)
The clause (إن شفائي ...) is declarative and the clause (وهل عند رسم ...) is a performative clause conjoined to the declarative; and the saying of another:
تناغي غزالا عند باب ابن عامر ... وكحّل مآقيك الحسان بإثمد
(You murmur to a gazelle at the gate of Ibn ʿĀmir; and kohl your beautiful eyes with antimony.)
and the saying of another:
وقائلة خولان فانكح فتاتهم ... وأكرومة الحيين خلوكما هيا
(Many a woman said: "Khawlān, so marry their girl, and the noble one of the two clans is free for you both.")
Ibn Hisham rejected these statements, replying to Abū Ḥayyān: «As for what Abū Ḥayyān transmitted from Sībawayh, it is a mistake attributed to him. As for the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays, the interrogative has had its meaning turned to negation, as we mentioned. As for his saying «فانكح فتاتهم», it is conjoined to an omitted imperative understood from the mubtadaʾ, that is, "pay attention to Khawlān". As for «وكحل مآقيك» etc., it depends on looking at the verses before it; it may be conjoined to an implied command indicating the meaning, that is, "do such and such, and apply kohl", as is said of «لأرجمنك واهجرني» that the implied form is "so beware of me and leave me for a long while", because «لأرجمنك» indicates it.»

dervis-irab:22-33.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قَصِيًّا): far from her family.
(فَأَجاءَهَا): It is said جاء and أجاء are two dialectal forms with one meaning. The basic rule for جاء is that it takes one object by itself; when the hamza is added, analogy would require it to take two objects, except that its usage changed after the transfer, so that it came to mean "he compelled her to (do) such-and-such". Do you not see that one does not say جئت المكان وأجاءنيه زيد ("I came to the place and Zayd made me come to it"), as one says بلغته وأبلغنيه ("I reached it and he made me reach it")? A parallel is آتى, which is not used except for giving, and one does not say أتيت المكان وآتانيه فلان ("I came to the place and so-and-so brought me to it").
(الْمَخاضُ): the pain of childbirth. In al-Qāmūs: مخض يمخض (with the three vowels on the khāʾ in the imperfect) means, of milk, "he extracted its butter", so it is لبن مخيض and ممخوض ("churned milk"); مخض الشيء means "he shook it violently"; مخض الرأي means "he turned the opinion over and considered its consequences until the right course became clear to him"; and مخضت (with kasra on the khāʾ), تمخض (with fatḥa), said of a pregnant woman, with the verbal noun مخاضا (with kasra on the mīm) and مخاضا (with fatḥa on the mīm); also مخضت in the passive; and مخضت (with shadda on the khāʾ) and تمخضت, said of a pregnant woman, mean that her delivery drew near and labour pains seized her, so she is ماخض, and the plural is مخض (with ḍamma on the mīm and shadda on the khāʾ) and مواخض. The letters mīm and khāʾ together carry a nearly uniform meaning: they point to slipping, whence مخر البحر والماء ("it ploughed the sea and the water", i.e. cleaved through it with a sound), and مخط and امتخط, which are well known.
(مِتُّ): with kasra or ḍamma on the mīm. It is said مات يمات and مات يموت.
(نَسْياً): النسي, with fatḥa or kasra on the nūn, means "that which is forgotten" (المنسي), like الذبح meaning "that which is slaughtered" (المذبوح), and it is everything that deserves to be thrown away, cast off and forgotten.
(سَرِيًّا): there are two views on السري. First, that it is the man of lofty rank, from سرو يسرو, like شرف يشرف, so he is سري; it underwent the same weak-letter change as سيد, so its lām is a wāw. One says "he is سري, from السراة and السروات". Bashāma ibn Ḥazn al-Nahshalī said:
وإن دعوت إلى جلّى ومكرمة ... يوما سراة كرام الناس فادعينا
(If you call, one day, to a great matter and a noble deed, the chiefs of the noble people, then call us.)
Second, that it is the small stream, which suits "so eat and drink" (فكلي واشربي); its derivation is from سرى يسري, because the water flows (يسري) in it, so on this view its lām is a yāʾ. Labīd said, describing a wild ass:
فمضى وقدّمها وكانت عادة ... منه إذا هي عردت أقدامها
فتوسّطا عرض السري فصدعا ... مسجورة متجاورا أقلامها
(He went on ahead and made her go forward, and it was his habit, whenever she hung back, to push her forward. Then the two reached the middle of the stream's breadth and cleft a filled spring, its edges close together.)
He means that he went on behind his she-ass towards the water and put her forward in front of him. أقدامها is the subject (ism) of كان, and he made the verb feminine (with the tāʾ of كانت) because أقدامها has the meaning of "putting forward" (التقدمة); عادة is the predicate of كانت. التعريد is lagging behind and cowardice. فتوسطا means the ass and the she-ass (reached) عرض السري, that is, the side of the small stream, فصدعا, that is, they cleft عينا مسجورة, that is, a spring that was full.
(رُطَباً جَنِيًّا): الرطب (with ḍamma then fatḥa) is what has ripened of the unripe dates before it becomes dried dates; and الجني is faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, meaning that it has become fresh and fit for picking.
(وَقَرِّي عَيْناً): that is, "be of good heart, do not grieve, and put away what has saddened you". It is said قرت عينه تقر (with fatḥa or kasra on the ʿayn in the imperfect). There are two interpretations of describing the eye in this way. The first is that it is taken from القر, which is coldness, because when the owner of the eye is happy his tears are cool, and when he is sad his tears are hot; hence they say, in a prayer against someone, "may Allah make your eye hot" (أسخن الله عينك). The second is that it is from الاستقرار (settling), the meaning being that Allah gave him what makes his eye settle, so that it no longer reaches for anything else. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "وقرت العين (of the form ḍaraba) قرة (with ḍamma) and قرورا means it became cool with joy; in another dialect it is of the form taʿiba."
(صَوْماً): silence. One says خيل صائمة وصيام ("horses standing still"). He said:
خيل صيام وخيل غير صامتة ... تحت العجاج وأخرى تعلك اللجما
(Horses that are still, and horses that are not silent, in the dust cloud, and others champing the bit.)
It is also said that what is meant by صائمة and غير صائمة is "standing still" and "not standing still". And صامت الريح means "the wind became still"; صام النهار means "the day reached its midpoint"; and صامت الشمس means "the sun stood at the zenith". "I came to him while the sun was at its midpoint (في مصامها)". And "he grew old, so the women kept silent about him (فصامت عنه النساء)".
(فَرِيًّا): الفري is "the wonderful", from فرى الجلد (to cut the hide); and الفري is also "the monstrous thing", said of good and of evil; it is also said that it means "the astonishing" and that it means "the fabricated". The hadith describing ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb belongs to the first sense: "I never saw a genius whose work was so masterly" (فلم أر عبقريا يفري فريه). الفري is also cutting hide for stitching and mending. In al-Mukhtār: "فرى الشيء means he cut it in order to mend it, and its pattern is رمى; and فرى كذبا means he created it, and افتراه and اختلقه (he fabricated it), and the noun is الفرية. The words of the Exalted: «شَيْئاً فَرِيًّا» mean 'something made up, fabricated', and it is also said 'something monstrous'. أفرى الأوداج means he cut the jugular veins, and أفرى الشيء means he split it, so انفرى and تفرى mean it was split." Al-Kisāʾī said: "أفرى الأديم means he cut the hide in a way that spoils it, while فراه means he cut it in a way that mends it."

* I'rab:
(فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَانْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ مَكاناً قَصِيًّا): The فاء is a conjunction attached to an omitted clause, its implied form being "so Gabriel breathed into the opening of her garment, and she conceived him"; the secret of this immediate sequence will come in the section on Benefits. فانتبذت is conjoined to فحملته. وبه is a preposition and its genitive noun, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī aimed at its sky (i.e. echoed its sense) in a poem in which he praises ʿAlī ibn Mukram ibn Sayyār al-Tamīmī and describes horses:
كأن خيولنا كانت قديما ... تسقّى في قحوفهم الحليبا
فمرّت غير نافرة عليهم ... تدوس بنا الجماجم والتريبا
(As if our horses had long ago been given milk to drink in their skull-caps; so they passed over them without shying, trampling with us the skulls and the breastbones.)
He means that their horses did not shy away from them, as if in their youth they had been given milk to drink in the skull-caps of their heads, that is, the skull-caps of the enemies' heads. It was the habit of the Arabs to give their noble horses milk to drink. القحف is the part of the head that is joined over the mother of the brain; الجمجمة is the bone in which the brain lies. So they trod on their heads and chests and did not shy away from them, as though they had become familiar with them. التريب and التريبة are the singular of الترائب, which is the place of the necklace. Among the amusing errors: one of them undertook to explain this verse, and since he did not know the meaning of التريب he said, literally: "التريب and التراب are two dialectal forms of التراب." May Allah increase him in understanding!!
ومكانا is mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) or mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as has already been discussed; وقصيا is an adjective.
(فَأَجاءَهَا الْمَخاضُ إِلى جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ): The فاء is a conjunction of immediate sequence. وأجاءها is a past verb with a fronted direct object (the pronoun); والمخاض is the delayed agent; والى جذع النخلة are two (elements) attached to an omitted ḥāl. The secret of the definiteness of النخلة will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(قالَتْ: يا لَيْتَنِي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هذا وَكُنْتُ نَسْياً مَنْسِيًّا): يا is a particle of vocative and the one addressed is omitted, or يا is merely for drawing attention. ليت and its noun; and the clause مت is its khabar, and it is a verb and agent. The adverb (قبل) is accusative because it is annexed, and it is attached to مت, and هذا is the muḍāf ilayhi. وكنت: the واو is a conjunction; كان and its noun; and نسيا is its khabar; ومنسيا is tawkīd (emphasis) of نسيا because it has the same meaning, and you may also parse it as an adjective.
(فَناداها مِنْ تَحْتِها أَلَّا تَحْزَنِي قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا): The فاء is a conjunction; ناداها is a verb with a direct object and a latent agent referring to the angel or to ʿĪsā. ومن تحتها are two (elements) attached to ناداها, meaning "from a place lower than her place", or attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent, that is, "he called her while he was beneath her". أن is explicative (mufassira) because the calling has the sense of speech without its letters; لا is prohibitive and تحزني is jussive by لا. It is also permissible that أن be a maṣdar particle, with لا negative and تحزني accusative by it, and أن with what follows it in the accusative by removal of the preposition, attached to the calling; but the first is easier. قد is a particle of affirmation. جعل ربك is a verb and agent. تحتك is an adverb attached to an omitted element which is the second object of جعل, and سريا is the first object. The secret of the reason for the removal of grief from her by means of the presence of food and drink will come.
(وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ تُساقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَباً جَنِيًّا): The واو is a conjunction; هزي is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the removal of the weak letter, and the yāʾ is the agent; وإليك are two (elements) attached to هزي. As for بجذع النخلة, Ibn Hishām cited it in Mughnī al-Labīb as evidence for the redundant (zāʾida) bāʾ in the direct object, and most of the parsers hold this. But al-Zamakhsharī, after mentioning the redundancy view, said something to this effect: it is possible that he treated هزي as an intransitive verb, though it is transitive, and then made it transitive with the bāʾ, as an intransitive verb is made transitive, the meaning being "perform the shaking upon it". And تساقط is jussive because it is the response to a request; وعليك are two (elements) attached to تساقط; ورطبا is a direct object; وجنيا is an adjective. تساقط is transitive by itself, and one example of it (not a proof text, because al-Buḥturī's speech is not used as evidence) is:
فمن لؤلؤ تجلوه عند ابتسامها ... ومن لؤلؤ عند الحديث تساقطه
(Some of it is pearl she reveals when she smiles, and some is pearl she lets fall when she speaks.)
It is reported from al-Mubarrad that رطبا is the direct object of هزي and that the bāʾ in بجذع النخلة is for instrumentality, and the strain in this is not hidden, since what falls within the scope of the command is delayed after its response. The ways in which the bāʾ may be redundant will come in the section on Benefits.
(فَكُلِي وَاشْرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيْناً): The فاء is the "eloquent" fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), that is, "if all this is complete for you, then eat". كلي is an imperative verb and the yāʾ is the agent, and what follows is conjoined to it. وعينا is tamyīz (specification) of the agent, because it is transferred from it, since the original is "that your eye be cooled" (لتقر عينك).
(فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَداً): The فاء is a conjunction; إن is conditional, its nūn assimilated into the redundant ما; ترين is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). Its original is ترأيين, with a hamza which is the ʿayn of the verb, a kasra-vowelled yāʾ which is its lām, and another, silent yāʾ which is the pronoun yāʾ, and the nūn is the sign of the nominative. The lām of the verb was dropped because it was vowelled and what precedes it has fatḥa, so it was changed to an alif, which then met the silent yāʾ of the pronoun and was dropped because of the meeting of two silent letters. ومن البشر is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of أحدا; and أحدا is a direct object.
(فَقُولِي إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمنِ صَوْماً فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا): The فاء is the linking particle of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); قولي is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the removal of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the agent; إن and its noun, and the clause نذرت is its khabar, and the clause is the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl). A difficulty will arise which we have answered in the section on Benefits. وللرحمن are two (elements) attached to نذرت, and صوما is a direct object. فلن: the فاء is resumptive and لن is a particle of negation, accusative-causing and of the future; أكلم is accusative by لن; واليوم is an adverb attached to أكلم; وإنسيا is a direct object.
(فَأَتَتْ بِهِ قَوْمَها تَحْمِلُهُ قالُوا يا مَرْيَمُ لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْئاً فَرِيًّا): The فاء is resumptive; أتت is a verb with a latent agent, and the tāʾ is for the feminine. As for به, Abū al-Baqāʾ attached it to an omitted ḥāl, "accompanied by him", which is good, but we see no obstacle to attaching it to أتت. وقومها is a direct object; and the clause تحمله is a second ḥāl, either from the pronoun of Maryam or from the pronoun of ʿĪsā in به. قالوا is a verb and agent; يا is a vocative particle and مريم is the one addressed; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of affirmation; جئت is a verb and agent; وشيئا is a direct object, meaning "you have done something"; وفريا is a naʿt. It is also permissible to parse شيئا as a maṣdar, that is, "a strange kind of coming".
(يا أُخْتَ هارُونَ ما كانَ أَبُوكِ امْرَأَ سَوْءٍ وَما كانَتْ أُمُّكِ بَغِيًّا): يا is a vocative particle, and أخت هارون is the one addressed, in a muḍāf construction, meaning "O one resembling him". Hārūn is a righteous man whom they likened her to in her chastity and righteousness; what is meant is not brotherhood of descent. It is also said that they meant Hārūn the brother of Mūsā because she was of his offspring, and the Arabs say to a man of Tamīm "O brother of Tamīm"; and it has been said otherwise, as you will see in the longer works. ما is negative; كان أبوك امرأ سوء: كان with its noun and khabar; وما كانت أمك بغيا is conjoined to the clause before it, meaning: "Since you are in this position of being expected to be chaste and righteous, from where do you have this child?"
(فَأَشارَتْ إِلَيْهِ قالُوا كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَنْ كانَ فِي الْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا): The فاء is a conjunction; أشارت is a verb with a latent agent; وإليه are two (elements) attached to أشارت. قالوا is a verb and agent; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; نكلم is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "we"; من is a relative noun, a direct object; the clause كان is the ṣila (relative clause), and the noun of كان is latent, its implied form being "he"; وفي المهد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; وصبيا is the khabar of كان. We have taken كان in its basic usage as the defective verb (nāqiṣa), indicating the conjunction of the content of the sentence with past time without any reference to its ceasing, as in the words of the Exalted: «وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً». A dispute has arisen among the scholars of Arabic about "كان" here, which we set out at length in the section on Benefits for the benefits it contains.
(قالَ: إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ آتانِيَ الْكِتابَ وَجَعَلَنِي نَبِيًّا): The clause إني عبد الله is the quoted speech, and therefore the hamza of إن has kasra because it occurs after "said"; إن and its noun, and عبد الله is its khabar. He described himself with eight attributes, the first being servitude. The clause آتاني الكتاب is a ḥāl clause, and this is the second attribute; والكتاب is a second direct object. وجعلني نبيا: a past verb with a latent agent and its two objects, and this is the third attribute.
(وَجَعَلَنِي مُبارَكاً أَيْنَ ما كُنْتُ): وجعلني مباركا is conjoined to وجعلني نبيا, and this is the fourth attribute. وأينما is a conditional noun that jusses, in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place; the response is omitted, indicated by what has gone before, that is, "wherever I am, He has made me blessed", and it is attached to the omitted response. كان is complete (tāmma) and the tāʾ is its agent; it is also permissible that it be the defective verb, with أينما attached to an omitted fronted khabar.
(وَأَوْصانِي بِالصَّلاةِ وَالزَّكاةِ ما دُمْتُ حَيًّا): ما دمت: ما is a maṣdar particle of duration; دمت is a defective past verb and the tāʾ is its noun; وحيا is its khabar; and the interpreted maṣdar is accusative as an adverb, and the adverb is attached to أوصاني. This is the fifth attribute.
(وَبَرًّا بِوالِدَتِي وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنِي جَبَّاراً شَقِيًّا): وبرا (with fatḥa on the bāʾ) is conjoined by nasaq (sequential conjunction) to مباركا, that is, "and He made me dutiful". He made his own self "dutiful" (barran) because of the extremity of his dutifulness. You may also make it accusative by an implied verb meaning أوصاني, to avoid a long separation. This is the sixth attribute. وبوالدتي are two (elements) attached to برا. ولم يجعلني is conjoined to وجعلني; وجبارا is a second direct object; وشقيا is an adjective, and this is the seventh attribute.
(وَالسَّلامُ عَلَيَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدْتُ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّا): السلام is a mubtadaʾ and علي is its khabar. There is a disagreement over the meaning of the "al-" attached to السلام. It is said that it is for the previously known (ʿahd), because the mention of the greeting directed to Yaḥyā has preceded, so it is directed to him as well. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The correct view is that this definiteness is an allusion, in language, aimed at those who accused Maryam, peace be upon her, and at her enemies among the Jews. The verification of this is that the lām is generic; and when he says 'and the genus of peace is upon me in particular', he alludes that its opposite is upon you. A parallel is the words of the Exalted: «وَالسَّلامُ عَلَى مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الْهُدَى», meaning that the punishment is upon whoever denied and turned away. The setting was one of denial and obstinacy, so it is a fitting place for this sort of allusion." ويوم is attached to the sense of settling (istiqrār) to which علي is attached, and it is not permissible to make it accusative by السلام because of the separation between the maṣdar and what it governs. The clause ولدت is what the adverb is annexed to. ويوم أبعث is conjoined to يوم ولدت, and likewise يوم أبعث [Translator's note: the source repeats يوم أبعث here; the second mention was presumably meant to be يوم أموت]. وحيا is a ḥāl, and this is the eighth and last attribute.

* Rhetoric:
Definiteness (al-taʿrīf):
This concerns the definiteness of the palm tree beside which the labour pains came upon her. This definiteness is either of the kind of definiteness of names that have become predominant (al-asmāʾ al-ghāliba), like the definiteness of al-Najm and al-Ṣaʿiq, as though in that desert there was a palm trunk well known to people, so that when "the trunk of the palm" is said, that one is understood and not other palm trunks; or it is the definiteness of the genus, that is, the trunk of this tree in particular, as though Allah the Exalted guided her to the palm tree only in order to feed her from it the fresh dates which are the khurṣa (the food of the woman after childbirth) suitable for her; and because the palm tree is the least of things in patience with cold, and its fruit comes only from its pith; so because of its suitability for her, together with all the signs in it, He chose it for her and compelled her to it.

* Benefits:
1- A summary of the story of the birth of ʿĪsā in the noble Qur'an:
No book among the religious books has concerned itself with the birth of the Messiah, the defence of the purity of his virgin mother, and the praise of her excellence and her preference over all other women, as the noble Qur'an has. For there are in it, about the birth of the Messiah, peace be upon him, and his life and his striving in the path of calling to Allah and reforming mankind, a number of verses in a number of surahs. It has come, concerning the innocence of the Virgin and her devotion, with what other books have not brought. Indeed the second great surah of the noble Qur'an is Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, and ʿImrān is the father of the Virgin, who was a scholar of religion; and no surah has come named after a lady of history other than Maryam, which contains a number of verses on the birth of the Messiah, as other verses have also come on this great event.
Allah chose the family of ʿImrān as He chose Adam, Nūḥ and the family of Ibrāhīm over all the worlds. ʿImrān, the father of Maryam, was a pious, scrupulous man, as his wife was righteous and pious. When she became pregnant she vowed to Allah that what she carried would be a servant of the Temple. When she gave birth and it became clear to her that it was a female, and the male is not like the female, her mother named her Maryam, but Allah accepted her in the Temple with gracious acceptance and caused her to grow in a good growth.
ʿImrān did not live until Maryam grew and became older, but died while she was small, and the husband of her maternal aunt, the Prophet Zakariyyā, took her in his charge. Maryam was truthful and blessed; Allah poured out His provision upon her from where she knew and where she did not know. Whenever Zakariyyā entered upon her in the prayer-chamber he found with her abundant provision, and would ask her, saying: "O Maryam, from where do you have this?", and she would answer him: "It is from Allah."
Maryam used to worship in the Temple, far from her family and from people, having withdrawn to an eastern place in Nazareth, of the city of Galilee. She was betrothed to a man of her cousins, named Joseph the Carpenter, but their marriage was not completed because she had dedicated herself to Allah. But Allah the Exalted willed to grant to mankind, from this pure, noble, pious girl, a noble prophet and a great messenger, and to make of her and of her son a sign for the people, as the Exalted said: «وَجَعَلْنَا ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ آيَةً وَآوَيْناهُما إِلى رَبْوَةٍ ذاتِ قَرارٍ وَمَعِينٍ». The marriage of Joseph to Maryam was not completed, and Allah sent Gabriel, who gave her the glad tidings of her conceiving the Lord Messiah while she was in her seclusion worshipping Allah and devoting to Him worship and piety. She was amazed at that and startled and said: how can I have a child when no human being has touched me? The answer to her was as it came in the Qur'an, just as the Qur'an portrayed Maryam's fright in Sūrat «Maryam» when the angel came to her with this glad tiding, appearing to her in the form of a human being in her seclusion, at a moment when she was off her guard, and she sought refuge with Allah from him. He calmed her fear and informed her that he was sent from heaven to give her a pure boy; so there came in this surah «واذكر في الكتاب مريم» etc. of the verses. The Gospel of Luke, the Gospel of Barnabas and the noble Qur'an agree, on the event of the birth of the Messiah, that he was a sign for the people and was not the result of Maryam's union with her fiancé Joseph the Carpenter, as is stated in some other gospels, such as the Gospel of Matthew, which states that "Jesus is the son of Joseph the Carpenter, son of Jacob, son of Matthan, son of Eleazar, son of Judah (al-Yahūd), son of Akhim", up to the end of this genealogy, which reaches Jacob son of Isaac son of Ibrāhīm, peace be upon them.
The noble Qur'an came down stating that Maryam was a virgin, and that after the angel's glad tidings to her of this pure boy she conceived him and withdrew to a place far from people, and suffered alone the pains of delivering him until she wished for death before this, as it came in the noble Qur'an «فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَانْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ» etc. of the verses. This noble newborn addressed her in his cradle and calmed her fear, and asked her to seek help for her weakness in the ripe fresh dates and the wholesome water; or the angel addressed her.
What Maryam feared then happened, of being accused of evil; when she came to her people with him they denounced her and accused her of what she was innocent of. So she kept silent from speaking, and the little child in his cradle undertook the defence of his pure, spotless mother, as it came in the noble Qur'an.

2- The secrets of the fāʾs:
We promised you that we would speak about the secrets of the fāʾs in the words of the Exalted «فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَانْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ مَكاناً قَصِيًّا فَأَجاءَهَا الْمَخاضُ». In these fāʾs is evidence that her conceiving him and her giving birth to him (took place at once): He conjoined the conceiving, the withdrawing to the place she went to, and the labour pains, which is the birth-pang, with the fāʾ, which is for immediacy. Had she been like other women, He would have conjoined with thumma, which is for delay and respite. Do you not see that it came in another place: «قُتِلَ الْإِنْسانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ، مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ، مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ، ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ»? Since between His determining him in the womb and bringing him out there was a stretched-out period, He conjoined that with thumma. This is in contrast to the story of Maryam, peace be upon her, for it is conjoined with the fāʾ. People have differed about the length of her pregnancy. It was said that it was like the pregnancy of other women; it was said, no, rather it was three days; it was said, less; it was said, more. This verse removes the disagreement, because it indicates explicitly that the conception and the delivery were close together, immediately, without delay, and perhaps that was in one day or less, taking what the verse indicates. This is what is reported in al-Mathal al-Sāʾir of Ibn al-Athīr. Ibn Abī al-Ḥadīd refuted this in al-Falak al-Dāʾir with what we reported in Sūrat al-Naḥl, namely that immediate succession is according to what is sound either rationally or by custom, until he says: "The fāʾ is not for real immediacy, whose meaning is that this occurs after that with no interval and no time, as this man imagined. Do you not see the words of the Exalted «لا تَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً فَيُسْحِتَكُمْ بِعَذابٍ»? The punishment is delayed after the fabrication. So the words of the Exalted in the story of Maryam do not indicate that the conception and the labour were in one day."

I said:
I said: Ibn Abī al-Ḥadīd's discussion is well directed, and what Ibn al-Athīr said is not free of weakness. The commentators have differed on the length of her pregnancy. Ibn ʿAbbās said nine months, as with all women; ʿAṭāʾ, Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said seven months; Ibn ʿAbbās also said in a single hour; another said eight months; others said six months; and others said three hours. The Imam al-Rāzī preferred that it was in one hour and said: "It is possible to argue for this in two ways", and he mentioned in the first way what Ibn al-Athīr said, and mentioned in the second way: "Allah the Exalted said in describing him: «إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَى عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ خَلَقَهُ مِنْ تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ», so it is established that ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, when Allah said to him 'Be', was; and for this a period of pregnancy cannot be conceived; that period is understood only for one who is generated from a sperm-drop."
The Shāfiʿī school holds that the longest period of pregnancy is four years and the shortest six months. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim was born after sixteen months; Shuʿba was born after two years; Harim ibn Sinān was born after four years, and for that reason was named Harim; Mālik ibn Anas was carried for more than three years; al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf was born after thirty months, and it is said that he used to say: "Remember the night of my birth"; it is said that ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān was carried for six months; and al-Shāfiʿī was carried for four years or less. The Ḥanafīs say to the Shāfiʿīs: "Your imam did not dare to come into existence until our imam had died", and the Shāfiʿīs answer them: "Rather, your imam did not stand firm before the appearance of ours."

The decisive word on the conjunctive fāʾ:
The fāʾ in its original placement is for connected sequence, and sequence is of two kinds:
1- Sequence in meaning: that what is conjoined by it follows directly without delay, as in the words of the Exalted «خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ»; and most often what is conjoined by it is caused by what precedes it, as in your saying: أملته فمال ("I inclined him and he inclined") and أقمته فقام ("I stood him up and he stood").
2- Sequence in mention: and it is of two kinds. One is the conjoining of a detailed statement to a summary that is the same as it in meaning, as in your saying: توضأ فغسل وجهه ويديه ومسح رأسه ورجليه ("He performed ablution, and washed his face and hands and wiped his head and feet"), and of it are the words of the Exalted: «وَنادى نُوحٌ رَبَّهُ فَقالَ: رَبِّ إِنَّ ابْنِي مِنْ أَهْلِي ...» to the end of the verse.
And it is a conjunction merely for sharing the ruling, such that the wāw would be good in its place, as in the words of Imruʾ al-Qays: «بين الدخول فحومل» ("between al-Dakhūl and Ḥawmal").
The fāʾ is specific in conjoining what is not fit to be a ṣila to what is a ṣila, as in your saying: الذي يطير فيغضب زيد الذباب ("the one that flies, so Zayd gets angry, is the fly"). Were you to put a wāw in place of the fāʾ, or another particle, and say الذي يطير ويغضب زيد, or ثم يغضب زيد الذباب, the problem would not be permissible, because يغضب زيد is a clause with no pronoun referring back to الذي, so it is not fit to be conjoined to the ṣila, since the condition for what is conjoined to a ṣila is that it be fit to occur as a ṣila. If the conjunction is with the fāʾ this is not required, because it makes what follows it together with what precedes it in the ruling of a single clause, by its indicating causation, as if you said: "the one that, if it flies, Zayd gets angry, is the fly" [Translator's note: the source text reads «الذي ان يطر يغضب زيد الذباب» and «دلك» for ذلك; translated as the sense requires]. Conjunction with the fāʾ may also be with delay, as in the words of the Exalted «وَالَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعى فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أَحْوى», either by assuming a connected (clause) before it, or by taking the fāʾ in the sense of thumma.

The eloquent fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa):
The fāʾ may be omitted along with what is conjoined by it if confusion is not feared, and likewise the wāw. An example of the omission of the fāʾ is the words of the Exalted: «فَتُوبُوا إِلى بارِئِكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ عِنْدَ بارِئِكُمْ فَتابَ عَلَيْكُمْ», the implied form being "so you complied, so He turned to you"; and the words of the Exalted: «فَمَنْ كانَ مِنْكُمْ مَرِيضاً أَوْ عَلى سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ», its meaning being "so he broke the fast, so he must make up a number of other days". This conjunction on the omitted response is called by the masters of the science of meanings (al-maʿānī) "the eloquent fāʾ". The author of al-Kashshāf said regarding the words of the Exalted: «وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا داوُدَ وَسُلَيْمانَ عِلْماً وَقالا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ», its implied form being "so they acted upon it and knew the due of the favour and the excellence in it, and they said: Praise be to Allah."
The author of al-Miftāḥ said: "It is a report of what He did for them and of what they said, as if it were said: We did the giving, and they did the praising. This category is frequent in the Qur'an and is part of its eloquence; for this reason the masters of the science of meanings called it the eloquent fāʾ."
As for Ibn al-Ḥājib, he said: What counts is what is customarily reckoned as ordered without delay. Time may be long while custom judges in such a case that there is no delay, and it may be short while custom judges the opposite; for a long time may be considered small in relation to the greatness of the matter, so the fāʾ is used, and a near time may be considered distant in relation to the length of a matter which custom judges to occur in less time than it. What appears from the words of the group is that the use of the fāʾ for what is delayed in its time and occurrence from the first, whether short or not, is only by way of figurative usage.
Al-Jarmī said: It does not indicate sequence in places nor in rains, by the evidence of «بين الدخول فحومل» and "it rained on such a place, then such a place" when the falling of rain in both was at one time. The meaning of immediate succession was objected to with the words of the Exalted: «الَّذِي أَخْرَجَ الْمَرْعى فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أَحْوى», for the bringing forth of the pasture is not immediately followed by His making it dry, dark stubble (أحوى, that is, dry and black). The answer is in two ways:
a- That the clause فجعله غثاء أحوى is conjoined to an omitted clause, and the implied form is "so a period passed, then He made it stubble".
b- That the fāʾ stands in for thumma, and the meaning is "He made it stubble". The detail of that will come in its place.

3- Why did grief lift from her because of the presence of food and drink?
Here a question that may arise must be answered. The apparent sense of the speech indicates that her grief will lift because of the presence of food and drink, in the words of the Exalted: «فَكُلِي وَاشْرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيْناً»; and it is known that her grief was not because of that, nor did it arise from the loss of food and drink. But the secret in that is that the consolation and forgetting of grief did not come to her in respect of their being food and drink, but in respect of their being a dazzling miracle that foretells for her, refutes the falsehood of the people, proves their lying and their spreading of rumours, and proves that she was among the people of protection (ʿiṣma) and distance from suspicion, and that she was far from what they accused her of. Furthermore, matters outside the customary course can be only divine and for a wisdom we do not know; of that is her giving birth to ʿĪsā without a male; and this is among the wonders of styles.

Why was she forbidden to speak?
Another question may leap to the mind after all this, namely: Allah commanded her to refrain from speaking for two reasons:
a- That ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, be the one speaking for her, so that it would be stronger for her argument and a greater foretelling of the miracle, and thereby remove the factors of suspicion that led to accusing her of what is shameful.
b- Legislating the dislike of any disputation with the foolish. The poet aimed at the sky of this meaning when he said:
يخاطبني السفيه بكل قبح ... وأكره أن أكون له مجيبا
(The fool addresses me with every ugliness, and I dislike to be his respondent.)

4- The places where the bāʾ is redundant:
a- In the agent. Its redundancy is obligatory in the verb of wonder that comes in the form of the imperative, such as أحسن بزيد ("How excellent Zayd is!"), and the reason for the redundancy is the improvement of the wording. Its i'rab: أحسن is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on its end, the appearance of which is prevented by the place being occupied by the sukūn that occurs for the sake of the form; بزيد: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition and زيد is the agent, nominative with an implied ḍamma on its end, the appearance of which is prevented by the place being occupied by the vowel of the redundant preposition. It is usual in the agent of كفى which means حسب ("suffices") and which is an intransitive verb, such as كفى بالله شهيدا ("Allah suffices as a witness"). The bāʾ is not added to the agent of كفى which means أجزأ or أغنى ("to be enough", "to suffice"), nor that which means وقى ("to protect"). The first is transitive to one object, as in:
قليل منك يكفيني ولكن ... قليلك لا يقال له قليل
(A little from you is enough for me, but your little is not called little.)
and the second is transitive to two, as in the words of the Exalted «وَكَفَى اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الْقِتالَ».
Ibn Hishām said: "In the poetry of al-Mutanabbī there occurs the redundancy of the bāʾ in the agent of كفى transitive to one object. He said:
كفى ثعلا فخرا بأنك منهم ... ودهر لأن أمسيت من أهله أهل
(It suffices Thaʿal as pride that you are of them, and a time in which you have become one of its people is worthy.)
and I have not seen anyone criticise him for it." Ibn Hishām was hasty in this judgement, for Abū al-Baqāʾ criticised him for it in his al-Sharḥ al-Mumtiʿ on the Dīwān and went on at length in parsing the verse, and al-Maʿarrī also criticised him; we are not here to investigate that, so perhaps you may refer to Abū al-Baqāʾ's commentary and to Mughnī al-Labīb.
b- In the direct object, as in the words of the Exalted: «وَلا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ», «وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ» and the words of Abū al-Ṭayyib:
كفى بجسمي نحولا انني رجل ... لولا مخاطبتي إياك لم ترني
(It suffices as thinness of my body that I am a man who, were it not for my addressing you, you would not see me.)
c- In the mubtadaʾ, as in بحسبك درهم ("A dirham is enough for you") and خرجت فإذا بزيد ("I went out and behold, Zayd"), and كيف بك ("How are you?"): كيف is an interrogative noun, a fronted khabar, and بك: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition and the kāf is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ and in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. The kāf stands in for أنت because of the entry of the preposition, and the meaning is "how are you, if the matter has come about?"
d- In the khabar, and it is regular in the non-affirmative, as in ليس زيد بقائم ("Zayd is not standing") and «وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُ الظَّالِمُونَ»; and in other than the non-affirmative it depends on what is heard from the Arabs (samāʿ).
e- In the ḥāl whose governing word is negated, as in his saying:
فما رجعت بخائبة ركاب ... حكيم بن المسيّب منتهاها
(No riding-party of which Ḥakīm ibn al-Musayyab was the destination has returned disappointed.)
and in emphasis with al-nafs and al-ʿayn, as in جاء زيد بنفسه وبعينه ("Zayd came himself, in his very person").

5- An important discussion about كان:
The words of the Exalted «كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَنْ كانَ فِي الْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا». In parsing it we proceeded on the basis that it is the defective verb, its noun latent, its implied form being "he", and صبيا its khabar. Among those who parsed it so is al-Zamakhsharī. We promised to report the dispute that arose around it, for its curiosity and for the mental exercise in it:
As for Abū al-Baqāʾ, he parsed it as redundant, that is, "one who is in the cradle", and صبيا as a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition-phrase; the detached pronoun implied would have been attached to كان. It is said that the redundant كان has no latent pronoun in it; on this basis it does not need to assume "he", but the adverbial phrase becomes the ṣila of من. It is also said that it is not redundant but is like «وَكانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً»; it is said that it means صار ("became"); it is said that it is the complete verb and من means الذي; and it is said that it is conditional and its response is كيف.
Al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī, known as al-Samīn, said: There are several views about this كان:
a- That it is redundant, and this is the view of Abū ʿUbayd, that is, "how do we speak to one who is in the cradle", and صبيا on this view is accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun that occurs as the ṣila.
b- That it is complete, meaning حدث ("occurred") and وجد ("existed"), and the implied form is "how do we speak to one who existed as a child", and صبيا is a ḥāl from the pronoun in كان.
c- That it means صار, that is, "how do we speak to one who has become a child in the cradle", and صبيا on this view is its khabar. [Translator's note: the source labels this item with ح instead of ج.]
d- That it is the defective verb in its basic usage, in its indicating the conjunction of the content of the sentence with past time without reference to its ceasing, as in the words of the Exalted «وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُوراً رَحِيماً»; for this reason it is expressed as being synonymous with لم يزل ("he has not ceased").
Ibn al-Anbārī said in Asrār al-ʿArabiyya: كان here is complete and صبيا is accusative as a ḥāl, and it is not permissible that it be defective because there is nothing specific to ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, in that, since everyone was in the cradle as a child, and there is nothing wonderful in speaking to one who in the past was in the state of childhood.
After writing what precedes I came upon what Abū Ṭāhir Ḥamza said in a treatise of his which he named al-Munīra al-Muʿriba ʿan Sharaf al-Iʿrāb, and I transmit to you its gist, for it has merit and curiosity and supports what we held, that كان remains in its usual sense. He said:
"But the sound view is that the intention is to report now about their state, because they considered that great at the time of his being in the cradle, so it is as though he said: they considered it great to speak to a child who is in the cradle an infant; so the being (al-kawn) is from the wording of the reporter, not from their wording, like the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa describing gardens:
يظل بها الشيخ الذي كان فانيا ... يدب على عوج له نخرات
(In it the old man who had been decrepit spends the day, creeping on crooked, worm-eaten (staffs).)
He was not decrepit before his creeping but at the time of his creeping, so he mentioned the being (al-kawn) from the wording of the reporter."

I said:
I said: All this is a murmuring to no purpose; the best is what we chose and what al-Zamakhsharī chose, and next in rank is that it be redundant. As for assuming it complete, it is very remote, because ʿĪsā was not created in the cradle to begin with.

6- بغيا:
Its original is بغويا; the wāw and the yāʾ came together and one of them was preceded by a sukūn, so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and the yāʾ was assimilated into the yāʾ; otherwise, had it been faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, the tāʾ would have been attached to it. Al-Bayḍāwī said: "It is faʿūl from al-baghy; its wāw was changed and assimilated, then the ʿayn was given kasra by assimilation, and for that reason the tāʾ is not attached to it; or it is faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil, to which the tāʾ is not attached because it is for intensification, or for relation, like ṭāliq." Some said: al-baghy is specific to the feminine, so one does not say رجل بغي but only امرأة بغي; but some transmitted from al-Miṣbāḥ that one says رجل بغي just as one says امرأة بغي.

dervis-irab:34-40.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلِكَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ قَوْلَ الْحَقِّ الَّذِي فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ): ذلك is a demonstrative noun, a mubtadaʾ; وعيسى is its khabar; وابن مريم is a badal (substitute); وقول الحق is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, that is, "I have said"; or it is a maṣdar confirming the content of the sentence, as in your saying هو عبد الله حقا ("He is the servant of Allah, truly"). Al-Zamakhsharī preferred that it be accusative as praise, by an omitted verb whose implied form is "I praise". Abū Ḥayyān distinguished between the two parsings, saying:
"The accusative of قول as a maṣdar confirming the content of the sentence means: these reports about ʿĪsā son of Maryam are established truth, not attributed to anyone else, that is, that she bore him without the touch of a human being, as you say هذا عبد الله الحق لا الباطل ('this is the servant of Allah, the truth, not the falsehood'), that is, 'I say the truth' and 'I say the saying of truth'; so الحق is the truth (al-ṣidq), and it is a case of annexation of the qualified to the quality." And الذي is an adjective of القول if ʿĪsā is meant by it and he is called "a saying" (qawl) as he is called "a word" (kalima) because he arose from it; or it is an adjective of الحق itself. وفيه are two (elements) attached to يمترون, and the clause يمترون is the ṣila of the relative noun.
(ما كانَ لِلَّهِ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ مِنْ وَلَدٍ سُبْحانَهُ): ما is negative; كان is a defective past verb; ولله is its fronted khabar; وأن يتخذ is an interpreted maṣdar, the noun of كان; ومن is redundant; وولد is genitive by من in form, a direct object accusative in position; وسبحانه is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb.
(إِذا قَضى أَمْراً فَإِنَّما يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ): The parsing of its like has often preceded; we repeat the parsing of فيكون: the فاء is resumptive and يكون is nominative, that is, "so it is being"; and كان here is complete. It was read with the accusative of فيكون, by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation that occurs after a request.
(وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هذا صِراطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ): The واو is resumptive and the clause is a new sentence, and therefore the hamza of إن has kasra; it was read with fatḥa by omission of the preposition. إن and its noun, and ربي is its khabar, and ربكم is conjoined to ربي. فاعبدوه: the فاء is the eloquent fāʾ, whose discussion has preceded; واعبدوه is an imperative verb, agent and direct object. وهذا is a mubtadaʾ, وصراط a khabar, ومستقيم an adjective of صراط, and the clause is a ḥāl clause. The saying was called a "straight path" by way of likening it to the road that leads to salvation.
(فَاخْتَلَفَ الْأَحْزابُ مِنْ بَيْنِهِمْ): The فاء is resumptive; واختلف الأحزاب is a verb and agent; ومن بينهم is a ḥāl from الأحزاب, and the meaning is "while the factions were some of them" [Translator's note: the source text reads thus; the sense is presumably "while the factions were among themselves"]. For the detail of their disagreement and the kinds of their sects one should refer to al-Milal wa-l-Niḥal of al-Shahrastānī, to al-Faṣl fī al-Milal wa-l-Niḥal of Ibn Ḥazm al-Andalusī, and to the longer works.
(فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ مَشْهَدِ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ): The فاء is a conjunction; وويل is a mubtadaʾ, and it is permissible to begin with an indefinite noun because it includes the meaning of supplication; وللذين is the khabar of ويل; the clause كفروا is the ṣila; ومن مشهد are two (elements) attached to ويل; and مشهد is a maṣdar mīmī, that is, "from their witnessing", in the sense of their presence; it is also permissible that it be a noun of time or place.
(أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنا لكِنِ الظَّالِمُونَ الْيَوْمَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ): أسمع is a past verb that came in the form of the imperative, or it is indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the silent last letter; and the bāʾ is a preposition added to the agent, which came as a pronoun in the accusative or genitive, for the appropriateness of the bāʾ. The discussion of wonder has preceded in detail, and the wonder here is directed to those addressed. لكن is the lightened (mukhaffafa) form, inoperative; والظالمون is a mubtadaʾ and في ضلال a khabar and مبين an adjective. He placed the overt noun in the place of the pronoun to signal that their wrongdoing reached the utmost and exceeded the limit. ويوم يأتوننا is attached to أسمع and أبصر.
(وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْحَسْرَةِ إِذْ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ وَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): أنذرهم is an imperative verb, a latent agent and an object; ويوم الحسرة is an adverb attached to أنذرهم, but it is better that it be a direct object, that is, "make them fear the day itself". وإذ is attached to الحسرة, for a maṣdar made definite by al-, acts upon the explicit object, so how much more upon the adverb. It is also permissible that it be a badal from يوم الحسرة, so that it is governed by أنذر, and by that it is confirmed that يوم الحسرة is a direct object and not an adverb. وهم: the واو is circumstantial and هم is a mubtadaʾ and في غفلة a khabar; وهم لا يؤمنون is a ḥāl clause arranged together with the one before it. The two ḥāls are either from the latent pronoun in the words في ضلال مبين, that is, "they settled in manifest error in these two evil states", so the clause وأنذرهم would be parenthetical; or from the object in أنذرهم in these two evil states.
(إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَرِثُ الْأَرْضَ وَمَنْ عَلَيْها وَإِلَيْنا يُرْجَعُونَ): إن and its noun; and نحن is tawkīd (emphasis) of the noun نا, which has the meaning of نحن, because it has its meaning; the clause نرث الأرض is the khabar of إنا; ومن is conjoined to الأرض; وعليها are two (elements) attached to an omitted ṣila of من; وإلينا are two (elements) attached to يرجعون; and يرجعون is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. In the wāw of the words وإلينا you may make it circumstantial or a conjunction.

* Rhetoric:
Al-majāz al-mursal (loose figurative usage) in the words «لكِنِ الظَّالِمُونَ الْيَوْمَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ», the relationship being al-ḥāliyya (the contained for the container), and what is meant is Hell. So he used "the one that occupies" and meant "the place that is occupied", because error does not settle in it; rather it settles in its place. Likewise his words «وهم في غفلة»: heedlessness is not something one settles in either; rather one settles in the perils that cast their owners into heedlessness.
